During last month's inventory audit, we discovered that fourteen wireless microphones, six uplighting units, and two portable projection screens could not be located. Replacing these items will cost the company nearly $9,000. To prevent further losses, the following procedures take effect on October 6.

All equipment leaving the warehouse must now be scanned out using the handheld readers at the loading dock. The program, now entering its sixth year, brings researchers and practitioners from other institutions and from industry to Marwood for residencies of one semester or a full academic year.

This cycle includes two notable changes. First, thanks to an endowment gift from the Halverson family, the number of funded positions increases from six to ten, and for the first time two of these are reserved for practitioners — professionals such as engineers, curators, or public-health officials — who need not hold an academic appointment. Second, departments hosting a visiting scholar will now receive a $3,000 hosting allowance to cover office setup, event costs, and incidental expenses, addressing a burden that several chairs raised during last year's review.

Proposals must be submitted by the host department, not by the prospective scholar, and should include a statement of the scholar's planned project, a description of planned engagement with students — at minimum, one public lecture and participation in a seminar series — and a letter of support from the dean. Departments may submit up to two proposals; if both are funded, the second residency must occur in the spring semester to balance office availability.

The selection committee, chaired this year by Professor Aldous Wren, will announce decisions by February 6. Full guidelines are on the provost's office Web site.

With best wishes,
Eleanor Castellane
Provost

Savings from canceled events

questions.question: What is indicated about the two positions reserved for practitioners?
options: Applicants do not need to hold an academic post.
They are limited to one-semester residencies.
They were funded by the university's own budget.
They require previous teaching experience.
questions.explanation: 둘째 단락에서 실무자(practitioners) 몫으로 처음 배정된 2개 자리는 엔지니어, 큐레이터, 보건 공무원 같은 전문가를 위한 것으로 '학술 직위가 없어도 된다(who need not hold an academic appointment)'고 명시합니다. 체류 기간 제한이나 교수 경력 요건은 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.question: Why is the hosting allowance being introduced?
options: To respond to concerns raised by department chairs
To attract scholars from foreign universities
To replace the program's lecture requirement
To compensate for reduced office space
questions.explanation: 둘째 단락에서 $3,000의 호스팅 지원금은 사무 공간 마련, 행사 비용 등을 충당하기 위한 것으로, '작년 검토 과정에서 여러 학과장이 제기한 부담을 해소하기 위한 것(addressing a burden that several chairs raised during last year's review)'이라고 설명합니다.

questions.question: What is true if a department has two proposals funded?

One residency must take place in the spring.
It cannot apply again the following year.
Both scholars must share one office.
questions.explanation: 셋째 단락에서 학과당 최대 2건을 제출할 수 있으며, '둘 다 선정되면 사무 공간 배분을 위해 두 번째 체류는 봄 학기에 이뤄져야 한다(the second residency must occur in the spring semester)'고 명시합니다. 지원금 포기, 차년도 지원 금지, 사무실 공유 의무는 언급되지 않았습니다.
